passage:
A restored city gate stood between modern shops and busy roads. Cars passed around it, and people took photos beneath it.
Students visiting the gate learned that it had once controlled who entered the old city. Merchants, soldiers, visitors, and residents all passed through.
Now the gate no longer stopped anyone. It invited people to remember that the city once had walls.
The teacher asked students what gates mean today. They discussed passwords, borders, school entrances, and social barriers.
The old gate became a metaphor. Some gates are stone. Others are rules, money, language, or technology.
